status_summary: Authority for SBIR and STTR lapsed after 2025-09-30 for about six months; S. 3971, the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act, passed the Senate by voice vote on 2026-03-03 and the House 345-41 on 2026-03-17 and was signed on 2026-04-13 as Public Law 119-83, extending the programs through 2031-09-30. The enacted text leaves the 3.2 percent SBIR and 0.45 percent STTR set-asides unchanged, adds security-risk screening, proposal limits from FY2027 and a strategic breakthrough allocation of up to 0.50 percent of an agency's extramural R&D budget drawn from its existing SBIR allocation, and contains no requirement to spend SBIR funds on U.S.-based capital investment; CRS describes the same provisions. SBA published a notice on 2026-09-02 setting updated commercialization standards for repeat awardees, effective 2026-11-15 per the notice. Of the chapter's three asks, continuation is met by statute, while the set-aside increase and the U.S.-spending rule were not found as of 2026-10-21.

timeline.event: Statutory authority for SBIR and STTR expires under the 2022 extension law; CRS later describes a lapse of about six months (exact start date not stated in the CRS product).
S. 3971, the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act, is introduced in the Senate and passed the same day without amendment by voice vote.
The House passes S. 3971 without amendment, 345-41 (Roll no. 89), under suspension of the rules; the bill is presented to the President on 2026-04-02.

Public Law 119-83 (S. 3971), the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act, is approved. Sec. 9 moves the SBIR and STTR authorization end date in 15 U.S.C. 638 from 2025 to 2031-09-30 and Sec. 10 extends related pilots to 2031; the text read leaves the 3.2 percent SBIR and 0.45 percent STTR set-asides unchanged, adds a Sec. 3 'strategic breakthrough allocation' of up to 0.50 percent of an agency's extramural R&D budget drawn from its SBIR allocation (agencies with SBIR spending above $100 million) for Phase II-follow-on awards of up to $30 million with a 100 percent match, adds Sec. 2 security-risk screening and foreign-ownership due diligence, and sets proposal limits from FY2027 (Sec. 4); it contains no requirement to spend funds on U.S.-based capital investment.

SBA publishes a notice setting updated commercialization benchmarks for repeat SBIR and STTR awardees (non-SBIR revenue share of 33 percent for FY2027 and 50 percent from FY2028), effective 2026-11-15 per the notice, with comments due 2026-10-31.
